query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small percentage of nickel (Ni) to the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEA) will improve its ductility and toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEA) with known mechanical properties.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of nickel (Ni) into the HfZrTi HEA.
generation.conditions: The alloy is subjected to standard mechanical testing at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: The addition of Ni is expected to modify the microstructure of the alloy, potentially leading to a more favorable phase distribution.
generation.mechanism: Nickel is known to enhance ductility in metallic systems by promoting solid solution strengthening and reducing brittleness through phase stabilization.
generation.predicted_outcome: The ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi HEA will increase with the addition of nickel.
generation.baseline: Current ductility and toughness levels of the HfZrTi HEA without nickel.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific range of nickel addition (e.g., 1-5 wt%) and does not account for other alloying elements or processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of improvement in ductility and toughness is uncertain and may vary based on the specific processing and microstructural characteristics.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare HfZrTi HEA samples with varying nickel content (0%, 1%, 3%, 5%) and conduct tensile tests.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of nickel does not result in a statistically significant increase in ductility and toughness compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
